medium_missing_id_followup_embedded_ord1.description: User opens a text chat asking for the latest on their package but does not give an order ID. Agent asks for the ID. User replies with a sentence containing a mixed-case, punctuated mock order ID and clarifies they won't share personal info. Agent calls lookup_order with the provided ID and returns status, ETA, and a tracking link.
medium_missing_id_followup_embedded_ord1.intent: A general user at home opens a text chat to ask, “What’s the latest on my package?” without sharing any order ID. They want a quick status update and an ETA, plus a tracking link if available. After the agent asks for the order ID, the user plans to provide a synthetic mock ID embedded in a sentence with mixed case and punctuation, e.g., “I think it’s order ‘ord-1002’?” The user stresses they’re only using tiny, non-sensitive mock data for calibration and do not want to share any personal info.
medium_missing_id_followup_embedded_ord1.title: User asks for package status without ID, provides mock ID in follow-up

actions.content: Hi — I uploaded a slightly cropped screenshot from another retailer that shows a product card for “Samsung 980 PRO 1TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2”. I can read a partial model string: “MZ-V8P1T0...”. There's also some tiny text that might say “without heatsink” but it's too compressed/blurred to be sure. I want you to find the 2TB version (same series) for under $120 on the tiny product search page. I'm not sure whether I need the heatsink — I'll wait for you to ask; if you ask, I'll confirm I want the heatsink version.

actions.content: screenshot_samsung_980_pro_cropped.jpg — Slightly cropped, compressed screenshot of a retailer product card showing title text 'Samsung 980 PRO 1TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2', a visible partial model string 'MZ-V8P1T0...' and a very small blurred line that could read 'without heatsink' but it's unclear.

actions.content: Thanks — I received the screenshot. I can extract the model/series from the image and then search for the 2TB listings. actions.content: Yes — please look for the heatsink version of the Samsung 980 PRO 2TB. Budget $120 is firm.

actions.content: Understood. I'll extract the model/series from the screenshot (partial model 'MZ-V8P1T0...') and search for 'Samsung 980 PRO 2TB with heatsink' under $120. I'll summarize the top matches and flag any over budget.

actions.name: Agent confirms parameters and runs product search

actions.content:
Search complete. From the screenshot I extracted the series as 'Samsung 980 PRO' and the partial model 'MZ-V8P1T0...'. 2) Samsung 980 PRO 2TB (no heatsink) — $169.00 — exceeds budget
3) Refurbished / open-box Samsung 980 PRO 2TB (with heatsink) — $129.99 — exceeds budget but closest to it

Summary: I didn't find any new 2TB Samsung 980 PRO (heatsink) listings under $120. The closest option is a refurbished/open-box at $129.99, which still exceeds your $120 limit. Would you like me to (A) set a price alert and re-check periodically, (B) expand the search to include other 2TB PCIe 4.0 NVMe models that may meet the $120 budget, or (C) look for used/third-party sellers that might list under $120?
actions.name: Agent summarizes search results and offers next steps

actions.content: Hey — I'm in a busy coffee shop so I might be hard to hear. Where's my package? I don't have the order number offhand.
actions.name: User asks for package status from noisy environment

actions.content: I can help with that. Could you give me your order number? If it's easier, you can paste the exact line from your confirmation email that starts with "Order #".
actions.name: Agent asks for order number and suggests pasting confirmation line

actions.content: Okay, hold on — here's the line from the email: Order #ABC-1234,
actions.name: User pastes confirmation line including hash, hyphen, and trailing comma

actions.content: Thanks — I see you pasted "Order #ABC-1234,". I'll look that up now using order ID ABC-1234.
actions.name: Agent acknowledges pasted line, normalizes order ID, and looks up order

actions.content: The order ABC-1234 is out for delivery — the carrier scanned it at your local facility this morning. The estimated delivery is today by 6:30 PM (typical delivery window 4:30–6:30 PM).
actions.name: Agent provides delivery ETA based on lookup result

where_is_my_package_no_id_coffeeshop.description: Young adult caller at a noisy coffee shop asks for package status without an order ID. Agent requests the order number, the user pastes the confirmation line exactly as in their email ('Order #ABC-1234,'), the agent normalizes the format, calls lookup_order, reports status, and the user asks for an ETA.
where_is_my_package_no_id_coffeeshop.intent: Young adult customer calling from a busy coffee shop to ask, "Where’s my package?" They don’t provide an order ID initially. After the agent asks for it and explains where to find it, the customer will copy-paste from their confirmation email something like: "Order #ABC-1234," (with a leading hash, a hyphen, and a trailing comma). Once the status is provided, the customer will follow up with, "When will it arrive?" seeking an ETA or delivery date.
where_is_my_package_no_id_coffeeshop.title: Busy coffee shop call: customer asks 'Where's my package?' then provides messy order line and asks ETA
